important.name: Per-id guidance rule for parallel splits is not in the agent's split procedure
important.summary:
todo-edit Step 2 (SKILL.md:45-53) dispatches one todo-editor per `--split` id, all carrying the same Guidance line, and says 'When the guidance names several ids, each agent applies only what it says about its own id, plus what applies to all.' Only the agent's `update` section carries that rule (todo-editor.md update step 2). The agent's `split` step 1 says only 'Guidance from the prompt wins.', and the skill's prompt block has no line telling the agent to filter, so a split agent dispatched for `todo-m3x9` with guidance `m3x9 one part per module; k7qf split by layer` is told by its own procedure to obey the whole guidance. The skill promises a behavior the agent that does the work never specifies.

Also (docs): todo-editor.md:136-139 has each split run `lease acquire --wait 300` up to 3 times (900 s in all) and end the run on the third held-lease refusal. With N split ids dispatched at once (todo-edit SKILL.md:47-52), the last split waits for the N-1 critical sections before it: re-read, dry run, real run, dangling-prose edits, check and `lease release`. With a few slow opus splits that can exceed 900 s, and that split ends with a relayed refusal. README.md:35 and :442-443, todo_sync.md:61-63 and the release note promise that parallel splits 'apply one at a time' and do not mention the limit. todo-edit Step 4 (SKILL.md:89) just relays each reply, and nothing tells the main session to tell the developer which ids did not split and need a rerun.
fix: In plugins/harness/agents/todo-editor.md `## split` step 1, after 'Guidance from the prompt wins.', add: 'Guidance that names several ids is shared by one agent per id: apply only what it says about this item's id, plus what applies to all.' (the same sentence the update section uses).
Optionally pin it in tests/skills/test_todo_edit_parallel_contract.py by asserting the sentence appears in both the split and update agent sections.

In todo-edit SKILL.md Step 4, add: a split reply that ends on the third held-lease refusal did not split its id; name those ids first and say to rerun `--split` for them. In the README todo-edit paragraph, add one clause saying a split waits up to 15 minutes in all for the lease, so a long batch can leave late ids unsplit.
Or cap the number of split ids one run dispatches (for example 3) in Step 1, and print the argument hint above it.

important.name: Theme toggle tests never run the deferred path that every real page takes
important.summary:
Both renderers inline pages/components/theme.js in <head>, where document.body is still null, so in a browser the toggle is always added through the else branch: document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", addButton). THEME_HARNESS in tests/lib/test_page_theme.py always hands the script a non-null document.body and makes addEventListener throw, so every node-run case goes through the synchronous `if (document.body) { addButton(); }` branch. Nothing checks the branch production uses: with it broken or removed, no test fails, but the theme button never appears on a rendered plan or TODO page.

Also (overall): theme.js is inlined in `<head>`, so on a real page `document.body` is null when it runs and the button is added only through `document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", addButton)`. The stubbed document in THEME_HARNESS always provides `body`, and its `addEventListener` throws, so every node test goes through the `document.body` branch. The deferred branch that real pages use is untested.

Also (system_shape): Both renderers inline theme.js inside <head> (page_chrome.theme_script; test_page_theme pins it there), where document.body is still null, so in a real page theme.js always takes `document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", addButton)`. THEME_HARNESS in tests/lib/test_page_theme.py stubs document.body as present and makes addEventListener throw, so every node case runs only the `if (document.body)` branch that a browser never reaches for these pages. The module docstring's claim that the toggle is placed under the brand at load is therefore untested on the path that matters.

Also (roast): `theme_script()` inlines theme.js in `<head>`, where `document.body` is still null, so in a browser the button is always added through the `DOMContentLoaded` branch (theme.js:32). The node harness in test_page_theme.py always provides a `body`, and its `addEventListener` throws `no body`. As a result every toggle test covers only the branch real pages never take, and a broken `DOMContentLoaded` path would still pass.

Attack: In plugins/harness/pages/components/theme.js, change the last line `if (document.body) { addButton(); } else { document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", addButton); }` to `if (document.body) { addButton(); }` (or change the event name to "load-never"). Then run `python -m pytest tests/lib/test_page_theme.py tests/lib/test_todo_snapshot_html.py tests/lib/test_plan_render_html.py -q` with node on PATH: every test passes. Open the rendered TODO_Snapshot.html or a plan _PIP.html in a browser: the script runs in <head> while document.body is null, the else branch is gone, and no #theme-toggle button is ever added to the .corner block.
fix: Add a THEME_HARNESS mode (for example data.deferred) where document.body starts null and addEventListener records the (event, handler) pair. Assert that the event is "DOMContentLoaded" and that the button exists only after the recorded handler runs (once document.body and .corner are set), placed under .corner.
As a no-node fallback, add a source-level assertion that theme.js holds `document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", addButton)` in the branch taken when document.body is null.
Add a harness mode where `document.body` is null and `addEventListener` records the listener, then fire it and assert the button lands in `.corner` with the stored theme already applied

Add a harness flag that sets document.body to null and records the DOMContentLoaded listener, then fires it and asserts the button lands in .corner with the stored theme already applied before the listener runs.

Add a harness mode with `body: null` whose `addEventListener(name, fn)` records `fn`; the test asserts the event name is `DOMContentLoaded`, then calls `fn` and checks that the button lands in `.corner` and still cycles auto, light and dark.

minor.summary: CLAUDE.md (Rules for changes, new config key) says a setting a driver can read and act on belongs in a config key and the driver, never in skill prose the agent must remember. The plan's D1A rationale cites the same project rule, yet the number a project would tune (a slow catalog, many parallel splits) has no key, and three documents must change together when it moves. Decision D1A was the developer's call, so this is a shape note, not a defect.

minor.name: Repo-name fallback depends on the local folder name, so the kept page differs between clones
minor.summary: When `todo.gh.repo` is unset, `repo_name` uses `main_worktree(cfg.project_root).name`, and the page puts that name in its `` and `<h1>`. The folder name is set per machine. Two clones in differently named folders draw different pages, so in a project that tracks `TODO_Snapshot.html`, each render on the other machine rewrites the page and shows it in `git status`. That works against the kept-page rule this PR adds to stop date-only churn. The README and release note present the fallback as equivalent to the configured name. Also (roast): With `todo.gh.repo` unset, `repo_name` falls back to `main_worktree(cfg.project_root).name`, and that name goes into the page `<title>` and `<h1>`. Two clones in differently named folders draw different pages from the same catalog. In a project that tracks `TODO_Snapshot.html`, each machine's render rewrites the tracked page with its own folder name. That defeats the kept-page logic this PR adds, whose release note promises the tracked pair stops churning. So the page stays stable across days but not across laptops. Also (adv_code_runtime): repo_name falls back to main_worktree(cfg.project_root).name when todo.gh.repo is null, which is the shipped default (plugins/harness/config/defaults.json:88). The name is drawn into the page's <h1> and <title>, so the rendered text depends on the folder each developer cloned into. Two clones with different folder names each see the other's page as differing from what they would build, so _kept_page returns None and render_snapshot rewrites the page with a new date and stamp even though the catalog did not change. This undoes the keep-the-page-when-unchanged behavior the PR adds, and it churns a tracked page between machines. Attack: Use a project whose .claude/harness.json leaves todo.gh.repo at its default null, with TODO_Snapshot.html tracked in git. Clone it twice at the same commit, as <dir>/proj and <dir>/proj-copy. In proj, run `todo_sync.py render --date 2026-11-01`; the page reads `<h1><span class="repo">proj</span>TODO Snapshot</h1>` and `<title>proj | TODO Snapshot (2026-11-01)`. Commit it and pull in proj-copy. In proj-copy, run `todo_sync.py render`: repo_name returns 'proj-copy', so build(header.rendered) no longer matches the page on disk, _kept_page returns None, and the page is rewritten with today's date and a new stamp. `git status` shows TODO_Snapshot.html modified with no catalog change, and render.json records `"wrote": ["TODO_Snapshot.html", "todo_live.js"]`. Running render again in proj after the next pull flips it back.
fix: Fall back to a value every clone shares (the repo name parsed from the `origin` remote URL), and use the folder name only when there is no remote
Omit the repo span when `todo.gh.repo` is unset, and say in the README that setting `todo.gh.repo` names the page
Derive the fallback from the repository, not the folder: parse the name from `git remote get-url origin` (strip `.git`), and use the folder name only when no remote exists.
Omit the repo line when `todo.gh.repo` is unset (`repo=None`), and say in the README and the `top_n`/snapshot docs that setting `todo.gh.repo` names the page.
Draw the repository name only from a configured value (todo.gh.repo), and leave SnapshotPage.repo None when it is unset, so the page text never depends on a local path.
Derive the fallback from something every clone shares, such as the repository name in the origin remote URL, and use the folder name only when there is no remote.

minor.name: put_updates lets a ranking ValueError escape as a traceback
minor.summary: put_updates converts only RankingError into TodoSyncError around apply_updates. apply_updates ends in reshape._rerank, which reads ranking_method and rescores every item, and a catalog-level fault there can raise ValueError. drain already treats that as a known failure: _probe catches (RankingError, ValueError) and _absorb_one catches ValueError. The driver's main() catches only ConfigError, TodoSyncError and OSError, so `inbox put --update` against such a catalog crashes with a traceback where drain would refuse cleanly. put's _validate (inbox.py:93) has the same narrow catch, but put_updates is new code and could have matched _probe.
fix: Catch (RankingError, ValueError) in put_updates (inbox.py:168) and re-raise as TodoSyncError, as _probe does; optionally widen _validate at inbox.py:93 the same way.

minor.name: A queued file holding both `updates` and `items` silently drops its items
minor.summary:
_holds_updates sends any object with an `updates` key down the update path, and read_spec(path, "updates") returns only that list. A hand-made or hand-edited inbox file that also carries an `items` list is accepted and deleted, and its add items never land; nothing reports them. put and put_updates never write such a file, so this only happens to a file written by hand, but the drain's contract is to apply or refuse each file, never half-apply it.

Also (roast): `_holds_updates` sends any object with an `updates` key to the update reader, whatever the value. Its docstring says that is deliberate, so a malformed value gets an update-spec refusal and does not fall through to the add path with a misleading `add spec` reason. No test queues `{"updates": "x"}`, `{"updates": []}` or `{"updates": [...], "items": [...]}` and asserts which reader runs or what reason the `.reason.txt` file gives. The fix this rule came from has no test to keep it from regressing.
fix: In _holds_updates (or _absorb_one), refuse a file whose object holds both `updates` and `items`, for example by raising TodoSyncError("inbox file holds both items and updates; queue them separately"), so it is set aside with that reason.
Or apply both lists from such a file: updates first, then add_items on the `items` list.

In tests/lib/test_todo_sync_updates.py, queue a file `{"updates": "x"}` and one `{"updates": []}` beside a good update, drain, and assert both are rejected with a reason naming `update spec` (or `at least one update`) while the good update lands.

minor.name: todo_sync.md exit-code table leaves out the OSError route to exit 2
minor.summary: plugins/harness/scripts/todo_sync.md:24-25 lists exit 2 as a configuration error, an unknown rule id, a refused operation, a held lock or a failed `gh` call, and says an unexpected error exits 1 with a traceback. `main` in plugins/harness/scripts/todo_sync.py catches `(ConfigError, TodoSyncError, OSError)` and prints `problem:` with exit 2, so a file-system failure (for example a failed inbox write in `put_updates`, which the inbox.py docstring says raises OSError, or a failed render write) exits 2 with a `problem:` line, not 1 with a traceback. A caller that tells the two codes apart from this table reads such a failure wrong.
fix: Add 'or a file read or write failure (OSError)' to the exit-2 row, and narrow the exit-1 sentence to 'any other unexpected error'.

minor.name: Driver docstring and todo_sync.md describe every command twice
minor.summary: The PR adds `plugins/harness/scripts/todo_sync.md` as the usage reference, guarded against the parser by test_todo_sync_usage_doc.py. It also keeps the full per-command reference in the `todo_sync.py` module docstring (lines 1-130) and edits both copies for `--update`, `--wait` and the kept page. Only the markdown copy is tested, so the docstring can drift without any check failing. Two manuals for one script means one of them will end up wrong.
fix: Cut the module docstring to its first paragraph (still used by `_summary()` for argparse) and a line that points to `todo_sync.md`.
Or extend test_todo_sync_usage_doc.py so every leaf command and option also appears in the module docstring.

minor.name: render subcommand help still says it always rewrites the page
minor.summary: The `render` subparser help reads "Rewrite the snapshot page and its stamp.", but `render_snapshot` now keeps a page that a re-render with its own date reproduces and writes `todo_live.js` only when its text differs. The module docstring, the `--date` help, todo_sync.md and the README all describe the keep-unchanged behavior, so `todo_sync.py --help` is the one surface that contradicts the code.
fix: Change the help to e.g. "Bring the snapshot page and its stamp up to date (an unchanged page is kept)."

minor.name: sync-gh-todo leaves out the same-drain condition on the overwrote part
minor.summary:
plugins/harness/skills/sync-gh-todo/SKILL.md:77-78 says the `overwrote <id> <field>` part appears 'when two queued updates set the same field'. `_absorb_updates` in inbox.py records an overwrite only against `(id, field)` pairs that an accepted file earlier in the same drain set, and the sibling texts say so: add-todo SKILL.md:84-85 and todo-edit SKILL.md:75-76 both add 'and both land in the same drain'. Two updates drained separately (for example by the todo-watch mod after each agent returns) overwrite silently.

Also (skill_package): add-todo Step 4, sync-gh-todo Step 3 and todo-edit Step 3 describe the same `add --inbox` output, but sync-gh-todo drops the qualifier 'and both land in the same drain' from the `overwrote` part (SKILL.md:77-78), which inbox._absorb_updates requires (only accepted files in one drain are compared), and phrases the landed-then-failed case as 'A `problem:` line opening `inbox: added` or `inbox: updated`' while the other two quote the exact form `problem: inbox: added <ids>; updated <ids>, then: <reason>` (inbox.drain's `_landed_text`). Readers of one skill get a different contract than readers of its siblings.
fix: Append 'and both land in the same drain' after 'set the same field' in sync-gh-todo SKILL.md, matching add-todo.

In plugins/harness/skills/sync-gh-todo/SKILL.md, append 'and both land in the same drain' to the `overwrote` sentence and replace the 'opening `inbox: added` or `inbox: updated`' sentence with the add-todo wording: 'When it reads `problem: inbox: added <ids>; updated <ids>, then: <reason>` (either part alone when only one kind landed), those changes landed ...'.

minor.name: argument-hint shows guidance as optional for `--update`
minor.summary: Step 1 stops the run on '`--update` with no guidance' and prints the argument-hint as the correction, but the hint ends with a single optional `[-- <guidance>]` shared by every operation, so the printed hint does not tell the developer what was missing. README.md:440 already writes the form as `--update todo-sp7t -- <what to change>`.
fix: Change the hint to `--retire ID[, ID ...] [--delete-retired] | --split ID[, ID ...] | --update ID[, ID ...] -- <what to change> | --refresh  [-- <guidance>]` (the parallel contract test's substring check on `--update ID[, ID ...]` still passes).

minor.name: todo-edit Step 3 drain-line grammar makes the updated part mandatory
minor.summary:
plugins/harness/skills/todo-edit/SKILL.md:73-74 gives the drain line as `inbox: [added N item(s): ...; ]updated M item(s): <id> (<fields>), ...; [overwrote ...; ][rejected K (<files>); ]check drift=<d>`, with `updated` unbracketed. `drain_lines` in plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/inbox.py appends the updated part only when `result.updated` is non-empty, so a drain where every queued update was refused but a queued add from another run landed prints `inbox: added 1 item(s): ...; rejected 2 (...); check drift=0`, a line the skill's grammar says cannot occur. The skill tells the main session to report each refused file's update as not applied, so the mismatch can confuse the report step. todo_sync.py's docstring and todo_sync.md:172 already bracket every part.

Also (skill_package): todo-edit Step 3 gives the drain line as `inbox: [added ...; ]updated M item(s): ...; [overwrote ...; ][rejected K ...; ]check drift=<d>`, with `updated` outside brackets. inbox.drain_lines (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/inbox.py, drain_lines) emits `updated` only when an update landed: when the queued updates are all refused but another run's queued add lands in the same drain (or the todo-watch mod already applied the updates and only adds remain), the line is `inbox: added ...; rejected K (...); check drift=<d>` with no `updated` part. The skill's own grammar does not cover that line, and the todo_sync.py docstring brackets `updated` as optional.

Also (system_shape): todo-edit SKILL.md:73-74 gives the drain line as `inbox: [added ...; ]updated M item(s): ...; [overwrote ...; ][rejected ...; ]check drift=<d>`, with `updated` unbracketed. inbox.drain_lines (inbox.py, drain_lines) emits the updated part only when result.updated is non-empty, so a --update run whose own update files were all refused while another run's queued add landed, or whose updates the todo-watch mod already drained before a queued add remained, prints `inbox: added N item(s): ...; [rejected K (...); ]check drift=D` with no updated part. The skill text then describes a shape the driver does not print; todo_sync.py's docstring and todo_sync.md (add --inbox row) bracket every part correctly.
fix: Bracket the updated part to match todo_sync.md: `inbox: [added N item(s): <id> (#N|note), ...; ][updated M item(s): <id> (<fields>), ...; ][overwrote <id> <field>, ...; ][rejected K (<files>); ]check drift=<d>`, and add that a line with no `updated` part means no queued update landed (each refused one is named in `rejected`).

Bracket the part like the others: `inbox: [added N item(s): <id> (#N|note), ...; ][updated M item(s): <id> (<fields>), ...; ][overwrote <id> <field>, ...; ][rejected K (<files>); ]check drift=<d>`, and add 'an update missing from the `updated` part was refused or applied by an earlier drain'.

Bracket the updated part in SKILL.md:73-74 (`inbox: [added N item(s): ...; ][updated M item(s): <id> (<fields>), ...; ][overwrote ...; ][rejected K (<files>); ]check drift=<d>`), matching todo_sync.md, and add that an update missing from the line was either refused (its .rejected.json) or already drained by the todo-watch mod.

minor.name: Step 4 omits the dropped-duplicate report that Step 2 assigns to it
minor.summary: Step 2 (SKILL.md:49-50) says to 'name the dropped duplicates in the Step 4 report', but Step 4 lists what to relay (each agent's reply, the Step 3 line, open items first) and never mentions duplicates, so a reader working from Step 4 skips them.
fix: In Step 4, after 'then the Step 3 line for an update', add 'and the ids Step 2 dropped as duplicates'.

minor.name: Id-cell loop passes vacuously on an empty row list
minor.summary: test_id_cell_holds_the_bare_id_for_copying iterates `zip(rows, IDS)`; if `_rows` ever matches nothing (a renamed row class, a changed `<tr>` shape) the loop body never runs and the test passes without checking any Id cell. The sibling tests index rows directly and fail loudly, this one does not.
fix: Add `assert len(rows) == 2` before the loop at tests/lib/test_todo_snapshot_html.py:255.

minor.name: Held lease not freed when the refusal assertion fails
minor.summary: test_acquire_refuses_once_its_own_wait_runs_out frees `held` only on the success path (line 77); a failing `pytest.raises` or timing assert skips the release. The project is a temp tree, so the leak is cosmetic, but the sibling test uses try/finally.
fix: Wrap the raises/timing block in `try: ... finally: locking.free(cfg, held)`.

minor.name: 'parallel' test runs its puts one after another
minor.summary: test_parallel_queued_updates_land_in_one_drain_with_drift_0 and the module docstring speak of agents queuing in parallel, but the two `inbox put --update` calls run sequentially in one process; the test proves two queued lanes drain together, not that concurrent puts are safe. The name overstates what is exercised.
fix: Rename to e.g. `test_two_queued_update_specs_land_in_one_drain_with_drift_0`.
Or run the two puts from two threads (as test_todo_sync_lease_wait.py does with a Timer) so the name holds.

minor.name: Usage-doc option check matches by prefix
minor.summary: test_every_option_is_named_in_its_command_section tests `` f"`{opt}" in section ``, so an option is counted as documented when only a longer option sharing its prefix is named (a future `--in` would pass on `` `--inbox ``). No collision exists in the current parser, so this is hardening of the guard, not a present miss.
fix: Match with a boundary: `re.search(rf"`{re.escape(opt)}(?![\w-])", section)`.

minor.name: Reply test name promises placement under Added, code checks presence only
minor.summary: test_the_agent_reports_queued_updates_under_added asserts only that `queued update` appears somewhere in the `## Reply` section; it would still pass if the phrase moved to another reply line (Retired, Notes). The agent's contract (todo-editor.md:267, :317) puts it on the `Added:` line, which the test name claims to pin.
fix: Select the `Added:` line of the Reply section (e.g. `re.search(r"^Added: .*$", reply, re.M)`) and assert `queued update: <id> (<fields>)` is in that line.
